units.function: Defines fully resolved, pre-ID-generated row shapes handed from the company portability orchestrator to chunked issue, comment, attachment, document and work-product writers.
units.dependencyDirection: A server-layer contract depends on shared enum/metadata types and mirrors database write shapes. The portability orchestrator produces it and persistence services consume it, so database concerns leak into migration orchestration.
units.keyDataModels: ImportIssueRow, ImportIssueCommentRow, ImportIssueAttachmentRow, ImportIssueDocumentRow and ImportIssueWorkProductRow.
units.lifecycle: Resolve slugs/IDs/statuses/assets before persistence; pre-generate parent and child IDs; batch insert rows; keep imported monitors unarmed.
units.testAssessment: No direct test owner exists for the type-only module. Previously completed portability and import-batching suites exercise consumers: 78/78 mocked portability tests passed, while the embedded-PostgreSQL batching suite was skipped and not claimed as passed.
units.designRationale: Avoid N per-row returning round trips and let child rows reference stable pre-generated parent IDs during bulk import.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS also needs efficient batch import, but mutation rows must be derived from a typed, digest-bound migration plan that retains source principals, responsibility/evidence identities and destination authorization decisions.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT as application-owned import commands and persistence-port DTOs. ADAPT pre-generated opaque IDs, resolved foreign keys and chunked writes, while keeping database row shapes and Paperclip shared types out of core/application.
units.responsibilityConflict: Attribution fields are nullable and optional by entity; issue rows have no responsible human or contract, comments carry local actor IDs without source identity, and evidence rows can lose creating run/source trust. No row is bound to importer, reviewed package digest or approval decision.

securityFindings: Record<string, unknown> adapter/workspace/metadata fields cross the persistence boundary without a typed capability or data-classification contract.
Most attribution and source-trust fields are nullable, permitting imported records with no accountable actor or provenance.
The row shapes contain no package/plan digest, source record identity, target revision or idempotency key.
Pre-generated IDs support efficient relationships but do not by themselves provide transactional or replay safety.
